title: Experimenting with Jev (system one AI) as an NPC
author: Tom_Baron
selftext:
This is my Full strategic turn based war game. You command a city amongst many in a two sided civil war. 

I wanted a little more dynamism in my NPCs, heard about Jev some time back and always wanted to try it out. So I wired the API into my dev server and got Claude to integrate it into my NPCs with a specific goal and strategy. 

Jev takes the role of the battle commander. The prompt to Jev gives a high level summary of the state of the city, the allied position and enemy position. Jev decides what to prioritise in each phase of plan -> attack and defence. Traditional NPC scripts and logic then execute what to do based on those orders. 

So it starts dynamically producing weapons based on how far away it is from its target city, decides whether to adopt a balanced, attacking or defensive stance and develops its city into a specialist attack defence or command centre hub depending on the role that evolves for it. 

Unfortunately its not currently as good as my meta bot 😆. Ill be working on that! But it is a fascinating experiment for something that id imagine will  become common in future games.

comments.author: Kill4meat
comments.body: I don't see this becoming a future of games. Maybe some niche ones. Jev or any LLM gives you semantic understanding. Do you really need it for game control? Game state is already numbers. Then you are converting it to prose, feeding to jev to get numbers again. Why make this step at all? It's a questionable use case.
